content.comment_body: We are planning to switch a 120W/230V induction motor directly using our [product_name]. Is there a risk of issues with the relay contactors? The switching frequency is about three times per minute. According to the datasheet, the contactors are rated for 100,000 cycles with a 3A inductive load.
I suggest using an external contactor rather than relying on the PLC's internal relay. With the rate you're operating—assuming 24-hour use—you'd likely need to replace the PLC after about a year.

I agree with the previous recommendation. There have been cases discussed in the German section of the forum involving defective relays, and replacing these relays can be difficult. It's best to use external relays and potentially a [product_name] module with 24 VDC transistor outputs. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members highlight concerns about relying on the internal relays of [product_name] to directly control a 120W induction motor at a high switching frequency. Reports of relay failures and the complexity of replacements are mentioned. Most users advise installing an external contactor to enhance reliability and extend lifespan in this application.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects to be able to reliably operate an induction motor directly with the internal relay of [product_name] without facing premature failures or complex maintenance, and hopes for the relay to last for the rated 100,000 cycles without problems.
